questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Fibres obtained from plant sources, such as cotton and flax, are classified as
questions.explanation: Vegetable fibres, such as cotton and flax, are natural fibres derived directly from plants.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Fibres obtained from animal sources, such as wool and silk, are classified as
questions.explanation: Animal fibres, such as wool (from sheep) and silk (from silkworms), are natural fibres derived from animal sources.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Cotton fibre is obtained from the
options: seed pod (boll) of the cotton plant
questions.explanation: Cotton fibre is harvested from the seed pod (boll) of the cotton plant, one of the most widely used natural vegetable fibres.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Flax fibre, used to produce linen fabric, is obtained from the
options: seed pod of the cotton plant
questions.explanation: Flax fibre is extracted from the stem of the flax plant, and is processed to produce linen fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Wool fibre is obtained from the
options: fleece of sheep (and some other animals)
seed pod of the cotton plant
questions.explanation: Wool is a natural animal fibre obtained from the fleece of sheep, and sometimes other animals like goats (mohair, cashmere).

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Silk fibre is obtained from the
options: seed pod of the cotton plant
questions.explanation: Silk is a natural animal fibre produced from the cocoon spun by the silkworm.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Fibres manufactured by chemically processing natural cellulose, such as wood pulp, into a new fibre form are classified as
questions.explanation: Regenerated fibres, such as rayon and acetate, are manufactured from naturally occurring cellulose that has been chemically processed into fibre form.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Rayon is an example of a
questions.explanation: Rayon is manufactured from cellulose (derived from wood pulp or similar sources), classifying it as a regenerated fibre rather than a truly synthetic one.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Fibres manufactured entirely from chemical polymers, without using naturally occurring cellulose as a base, are classified as
questions.explanation: True synthetic fibres, such as nylon and polyester, are manufactured entirely from chemical polymers rather than processed natural materials.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Nylon, polyester, and acrylic are all examples of
questions.explanation: Nylon, polyester, and acrylic are manufactured entirely from synthetic chemical polymers, classifying them as true synthetic fibres.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Examining a fibre under a microscope to observe its structure is one method used for
questions.explanation: Microscopic examination reveals a fibre's distinctive structural features, helping to identify the type of fibre present in a fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A test that identifies fibre type by observing how a small sample reacts when exposed to a flame, including the smell and residue produced, is called a
questions.explanation: The burning test identifies fibres based on characteristics such as how they burn, the smell produced, and the type of ash or residue left behind.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: When burned, natural cellulose fibres such as cotton typically produce a smell similar to
questions.explanation: Cotton and other cellulose fibres typically burn with a smell resembling burning paper, distinguishing them from protein-based fibres like wool.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: When burned, protein-based fibres such as wool or silk typically produce a smell similar to
questions.explanation: Wool and silk, being protein-based fibres, typically produce a smell resembling burning hair or feathers when tested by burning.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The ability of a fabric to withstand pulling force without breaking is called its
questions.explanation: Tensile strength measures a fabric's resistance to breaking under pulling (tension) forces, an important property for durability.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The ability of a fabric to take up and hold moisture is called its
questions.explanation: Moisture absorbency describes how readily a fabric takes up and holds moisture, affecting comfort, especially in warm climates.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A continuous, very long strand of fibre, such as that produced naturally by a silkworm, is used to make
questions.explanation: Filament yarns are made from continuous, long fibre strands, such as those naturally produced by silk, or manufactured synthetically.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A yarn made by twisting together many short fibre lengths, such as those from cotton or wool, is called
questions.explanation: Staple yarns are spun from many short fibre lengths twisted together, typical of natural fibres like cotton and wool.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The lengthwise yarns held under tension on a loom, through which the crosswise yarns are woven, are called the
questions.explanation: The warp consists of the lengthwise yarns fixed to the loom, forming the foundation through which the weft yarns are interlaced.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The crosswise yarns woven over and under the warp yarns on a loom to create fabric are called the
questions.explanation: The weft yarns are woven crosswise, over and under the warp yarns, to construct woven fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The simplest weave pattern, in which the weft yarn passes alternately over and under each warp yarn, is called the
questions.explanation: Plain weave is the most basic weaving pattern, with the weft simply alternating over and under each warp yarn in a regular sequence.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A fabric construction method that interlocks a series of connected loops of yarn, rather than weaving crossed threads, is called
questions.explanation: Knitting constructs fabric by interlocking loops of yarn, giving knitted fabrics their characteristic stretch, unlike woven fabrics.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A fabric construction method that matts and compresses fibres together using heat, moisture, and pressure, without weaving or knitting, is called
questions.explanation: Felting compresses and matts fibres (traditionally wool) together using heat, moisture, and pressure, producing fabric without weaving or knitting.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A fabric construction method that joins fibres together using an adhesive or heat-fusing process, common in non-woven fabrics, is called
questions.explanation: Bonding joins fibres together using adhesives or heat fusion, a technique commonly used to produce non-woven fabrics.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A chemical test used to help identify fibre type by observing how a sample reacts when exposed to acids or alkalis is called a
questions.explanation: Chemical tests expose fibre samples to reagents such as acids or alkalis, observing reactions like dissolving or discolouration to help identify fibre type.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Cotton fabric is generally known for its
options: inability to be dyed any colour
good moisture absorbency and comfort in warm climates
questions.explanation: Cotton is valued for its good moisture absorbency, making it comfortable to wear, particularly in warm climates.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Silk fabric is generally known for its
options: natural sheen (lustre) and smooth, luxurious feel
inability to be woven into fabric
questions.explanation: Silk is prized for its natural lustre and smooth, luxurious feel, making it a highly valued fabric for fine garments.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Wool fabric is generally known for its
options: good warmth retention, making it suitable for colder climates
unsuitability for any type of garment
poor warmth retention compared to cotton
questions.explanation: Wool is valued for its excellent warmth retention properties, making it particularly suitable for garments worn in colder climates.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Polyester fabric is generally known for its
options: durability, wrinkle resistance, and quick-drying properties
extremely poor durability compared to natural fibres
very slow drying time compared to cotton
questions.explanation: Polyester, a true synthetic fibre, is valued for its durability, resistance to wrinkling, and quick-drying properties.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A blended fabric, combining two or more different fibre types (such as cotton and polyester), is created mainly to
options: combine the desirable properties of each fibre type in a single fabric
increase production cost with no functional benefit
eliminate all properties of both fibre types
questions.explanation: Blended fabrics combine different fibres to bring together their most desirable properties, such as cotton's comfort with polyester's durability.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The narrow, tightly woven edge running along both lengthwise sides of a woven fabric, which prevents fraying, is called the
questions.explanation: The selvedge is the fabric's finished, self-edged border along its length, preventing the edges from fraying.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A twill weave, in contrast to a plain weave, is generally identified by its
options: distinctive diagonal rib pattern on the fabric's surface
completely flat surface with no visible pattern
inability to be used for any type of garment
identical structure to a plain weave in every respect
questions.explanation: Twill weave produces a distinctive diagonal rib pattern on the fabric surface, differing from the simple, flat criss-cross appearance of a plain weave.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Knitted fabrics, compared to woven fabrics, generally offer greater
options: similarity to felted fabric in construction method
stretch and flexibility, due to their looped construction
resistance to any form of stretching
questions.explanation: The interlocking loop structure of knitted fabrics gives them greater inherent stretch and flexibility compared to the fixed criss-cross structure of woven fabrics.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The part of a sewing machine that holds and drives the needle up and down is called the
questions.explanation: The needle bar holds the needle and moves it up and down as the machine operates, forming stitches through the fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The small case holding the bottom thread supply on a sewing machine, interlocking with the top thread to form a stitch, is called the
questions.explanation: The bobbin case holds the lower thread supply, which interlocks with the needle's upper thread beneath the fabric to form a stitch.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The part of a sewing machine that holds the fabric flat against the feed dogs during stitching is called the
questions.explanation: The presser foot holds the fabric firmly in place against the feed dogs, ensuring even, controlled movement of fabric during stitching.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The mechanism on a sewing machine that controls how tightly the thread is drawn, affecting stitch quality, is called the
questions.explanation: Tension control discs regulate how much resistance is applied to the thread as it passes through, directly affecting the quality and balance of each stitch.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Thread breaking frequently while sewing is often caused by
options: no issue at all with the machine's settings
incorrect tension settings or a poorly threaded machine
using thread of the correct weight for the fabric
questions.explanation: Frequent thread breakage is commonly caused by incorrect tension settings or improper threading of the machine.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Skipped stitches while sewing are often caused by
options: using a brand new, correctly inserted needle
a bent, blunt, or incorrectly inserted needle
questions.explanation: Skipped stitches are commonly caused by problems with the needle, such as it being bent, blunt, or not properly inserted into the machine.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Puckered seams while sewing are often caused by
options: excessively tight thread tension for the fabric being used
correctly balanced tension appropriate to the fabric
properly matched thread and fabric weight
questions.explanation: Puckered seams often result from thread tension set too tightly for the fabric being sewn, causing the fabric to gather unevenly along the seam.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A tool used to measure body dimensions and fabric lengths, typically flexible enough to follow body curves, is called a
questions.explanation: A flexible tape measure is essential for accurately measuring body dimensions and fabric lengths, including curved areas.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A marking tool used to draw temporary guide lines directly onto fabric, easily removable afterward, is called
questions.explanation: Tailor's chalk marks fabric temporarily, allowing guide lines for cutting or stitching that can later be brushed or washed away.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A cutting tool with straight blades used for cutting fabric cleanly along marked lines is called
questions.explanation: Shears have straight-edged blades designed for making clean, accurate cuts through fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A cutting tool with zigzag-edged blades, used to cut fabric edges in a way that reduces fraying, is called
questions.explanation: Pinking shears cut fabric with a zigzag edge, which helps to reduce fraying along raw, unfinished fabric edges.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A small tool used to unpick unwanted stitches from a seam is called a
questions.explanation: A seam ripper is specifically designed to carefully cut and remove unwanted stitches from a seam.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A small protective cap worn on the finger to push a needle through fabric safely during hand sewing is called a
questions.explanation: A thimble protects the finger while pushing a needle through fabric, particularly useful for thicker or tougher materials.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Temporary stitches used to hold fabric pieces together before permanent stitching, easily removed afterward, are called
questions.explanation: Tacking (basting) stitches temporarily hold fabric layers in place before final, permanent stitching, and are removed once no longer needed.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A basic hand stitch made by passing the needle in and out of the fabric in a simple, even, straight line is called a
questions.explanation: A running stitch is a simple, straightforward hand stitch, formed by evenly passing the needle in and out of the fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A strong hand stitch formed by taking the needle back over the previous stitch before moving forward, commonly used for durability, is called a
questions.explanation: A backstitch is a strong, durable hand stitch created by looping back over the previous stitch, providing greater strength than a simple running stitch.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A stitch specifically used to secure a folded fabric edge (hem) in place, often nearly invisible from the right side, is called a
questions.explanation: A hemming stitch secures a folded fabric edge discreetly, ideally remaining nearly invisible on the garment's right side.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A simple seam formed by placing two fabric pieces right sides together and stitching along the seam allowance, then pressing it open or to one side, is called an
questions.explanation: An open (plain) seam is the most basic seam type, sewn with fabric right sides together and the seam allowance pressed open or to one side.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A seam that fully encloses the raw edges within a second row of stitching, giving a clean finish on both sides, is called a
questions.explanation: A French seam encloses the fabric's raw edges completely, achieved by stitching twice, giving a neat, self-finished appearance on both sides.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A flat, enclosed seam commonly used in more durable garments like jeans, formed by folding one seam allowance over the other and stitching it down, is called a
questions.explanation: A machine-felled (flat-felled) seam encloses raw edges within a flat, durable finish, commonly seen in sturdy garments such as jeans.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Small folds of fabric drawn together by a line of stitching, used to control fullness in a soft, gathered manner, are called
questions.explanation: Gathers create soft, evenly distributed fullness in fabric, typically formed by pulling stitching threads to draw the fabric together.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A fold of fabric pressed and stitched in place to control fullness, folded in a single direction, is called a
questions.explanation: A knife pleat is a single fold of fabric pressed uniformly in one direction, commonly used to control fullness in skirts and garments.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A pleat formed by two folds turning away from each other, creating a flat panel in the centre, is called a
questions.explanation: A box pleat is formed by two folds facing outward in opposite directions, creating a flat panel of fabric in the centre.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A pleat formed by two folds turning toward each other, creating a flat panel that appears as the reverse of a box pleat, is called an
questions.explanation: An inverted pleat is essentially a box pleat viewed from the reverse side, with the folds turning inward rather than outward.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A stitched, tapered fold used to shape flat fabric to fit the contours of the body, such as at the bust or waist, is called a
questions.explanation: Darts are tapered folds sewn into flat fabric to create shape, allowing garments to fit the body's natural contours.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A small, stitched fold of fabric, similar to a pleat but generally narrower and used more for decorative or minor fullness control, is called a
questions.explanation: Tucks are small, stitched folds, narrower than typical pleats, often used decoratively or to control minor amounts of fullness.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A garment opening finished with a continuous strip of fabric, commonly used for openings like sleeve cuffs, is called a
questions.explanation: A continuous strip opening (placket) uses a folded strip of fabric to neatly finish an opening, commonly seen at sleeve cuffs.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A garment opening finished by attaching a separate, shaped piece of fabric to neaten the raw edges is called a
questions.explanation: A faced opening uses a separate shaped fabric piece (facing) stitched to the garment to neatly finish the raw edges of an opening.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A mechanical fastener with interlocking teeth, drawn together or apart by a sliding tab, is called a
questions.explanation: A zipper uses interlocking teeth and a sliding tab to quickly open and close a garment opening.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A fastener consisting of a small disc sewn onto fabric, secured through a corresponding buttonhole, is called a
questions.explanation: A button is secured through a matching buttonhole, one of the most common and traditional garment fastening methods.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A small metal fastener consisting of a hook and a corresponding loop (eye), often used at waistbands or necklines, is called a
questions.explanation: A hook and eye fastener uses a small metal hook that catches a corresponding loop (eye), commonly used at waistbands or necklines.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A small, two-part snap fastener that clicks together when pressed, commonly used on lighter garments, is called a
questions.explanation: A press stud (snap fastener) consists of two interlocking parts that click together when pressed, commonly used on lighter fabrics and garments.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A piece of fabric attached to the inside of a garment opening or edge to neaten and strengthen it, without being visible from the outside, is called a
questions.explanation: A facing is stitched to the inside of an edge or opening to neaten and reinforce it, remaining hidden from the outside of the garment.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A strip of fabric or bias tape used to enclose and finish a raw fabric edge, often visible on the outside of the garment, is called a
questions.explanation: Binding encloses a raw fabric edge using a strip of fabric or bias tape, often visible and sometimes used decoratively on the garment's exterior.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Taking accurate body measurements, such as bust, waist, and hip, is an essential first step in
questions.explanation: Accurate body measurements form the essential foundation for drafting patterns and ensuring a well-fitting garment.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A pre-printed pattern, purchased ready-made in standard sizes for home sewing, is called a
questions.explanation: Commercial flat patterns are pre-printed, standard-sized patterns purchased for home use, offering a convenient alternative to drafting from scratch.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A basic, fitted pattern shape without design details, used as a foundation for developing other pattern styles, is called a
questions.explanation: A basic block (sloper) is a simple, closely fitted foundation pattern, from which more elaborate designs can be developed by adding style features.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A basic pattern block covering the upper body torso area is called the
questions.explanation: The bodice block is the foundational pattern piece for the upper body (torso), used as a base for designing various tops and dresses.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A basic pattern block covering the lower body from the waist down to a chosen hem length is called the
questions.explanation: The skirt block is the foundational pattern piece covering the body from the waist downward, used as a base for various skirt designs.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A basic pattern block specifically shaping the arm covering of a garment is called the
questions.explanation: The sleeve block is the foundational pattern piece shaping the arm covering, used as a base for designing different sleeve styles.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Adjusting a pattern to better suit an individual's specific body measurements or fit preferences is called
questions.explanation: Pattern alteration modifies a standard or basic pattern to better match an individual's specific body measurements and fit needs.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The design principle concerned with the visual direction created by seams, darts, or trims on a garment is called
questions.explanation: Line refers to the visual direction created within a garment's design, such as through seams, darts, or decorative trim, influencing its overall silhouette.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The design principle concerned with the overall three-dimensional shape and structure of a garment on the body is called
questions.explanation: Form describes the overall three-dimensional shape a garment takes on the body, influenced by its cut and construction.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The design principle concerned with the hue and shade choices used in a garment's fabric or trim is called
questions.explanation: Colour, as a design principle, considers the hues and shades selected for a garment, influencing mood and visual impact.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The design principle concerned with the surface quality and feel of a garment's fabric, such as smooth or rough, is called
questions.explanation: Texture describes the surface quality and tactile feel of a fabric, contributing to a garment's overall visual and physical character.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: When selecting a garment for a formal occasion, an important consideration is
options: selecting only garments unsuitable for the weather
choosing styles and fabrics appropriate to the formality of the event
ignoring the nature of the event entirely
wearing whatever is most casual regardless of the occasion
questions.explanation: Selecting appropriate garments for an occasion involves matching the style and fabric formality to the nature of the event.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: When selecting garments suited to a person's body silhouette, the general goal is to
options: always choose the tightest possible fit regardless of shape
select only one universal style suitable for every body shape
choose styles that flatter and balance the individual's body shape
ignore body shape entirely when selecting clothing
questions.explanation: Thoughtful garment selection considers an individual's body silhouette, choosing styles that flatter and create a balanced, harmonious appearance.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Wardrobe planning that considers a person's financial allocation mainly aims to
options: select versatile, cost-effective garments that meet the individual's needs within budget
encourage unlimited spending regardless of financial means
ignore cost considerations entirely when planning a wardrobe
select only the most expensive garments available
questions.explanation: Budget-conscious wardrobe planning focuses on selecting versatile, cost-effective garments that meet needs while remaining within financial means.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Traditional soap, used in laundry work, is generally made through a chemical reaction between fat/oil and
questions.explanation: Traditional soap is produced through saponification, a chemical reaction between fats/oils and an alkali such as caustic soda.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Synthetic detergents, compared to traditional soap, generally offer an advantage in
options: being made entirely from natural fats and oils only
performing effectively even in hard water, without forming scum
being completely ineffective at removing dirt
questions.explanation: Synthetic detergents were developed partly to overcome soap's tendency to form scum in hard water, performing more effectively under such conditions.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The laundry step that involves separating garments by colour, fabric type, or soil level before washing is called
questions.explanation: Sorting separates garments by colour, fabric type, or soiling level before washing, helping to prevent colour bleeding and fabric damage.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The laundry step that involves submerging heavily soiled garments in water (often with detergent) before the main wash is called
questions.explanation: Soaking pre-treats heavily soiled garments by submerging them in water, often with detergent, loosening stains before the main wash cycle.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The laundry step that applies a stiffening agent to certain fabrics, such as cotton, to give them added body and crispness, is called
questions.explanation: Starching applies a stiffening agent to fabric, giving items like cotton shirts added body and a crisp finish.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: The laundry step that uses heat and pressure to smooth out wrinkles from freshly washed and dried garments is called
questions.explanation: Pressing (ironing) uses heat and pressure to smooth out wrinkles, giving laundered garments a neat, finished appearance.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Removing a stain using an appropriate chemical reagent generally requires first identifying the
options: brand of the garment, regardless of the stain type
colour of the garment only, ignoring the stain's nature
type of stain, since different stains require different treatment methods
size of the garment only, with no regard for the stain
questions.explanation: Effective stain removal depends on correctly identifying the type of stain, since different stains (e.g., oil-based vs. protein-based) require different treatment approaches.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: International textile care symbols, found on garment labels, are designed to
options: only apply within a single specific country
replace the need for any washing instructions at all
indicate the price of the garment
provide standardised washing and care instructions understood across different countries and languages
questions.explanation: Standardised international care symbols provide universally understood washing and care guidance, regardless of the language spoken by the garment's owner.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A care label symbol showing a triangle typically relates to instructions regarding
questions.explanation: The triangle symbol on care labels conventionally relates to bleaching instructions, indicating whether and how a garment may be safely bleached.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A care label symbol showing a circle typically relates to instructions regarding
questions.explanation: The circle symbol on care labels conventionally indicates dry cleaning instructions, including whether the garment is suitable for this process.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A care label symbol showing an iron shape typically relates to instructions regarding
questions.explanation: The iron-shaped symbol on care labels conventionally indicates the appropriate ironing temperature and any precautions for the fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A care label symbol showing a tub or basin shape typically relates to instructions regarding
questions.explanation: The tub (washtub) symbol on care labels conventionally indicates appropriate washing temperature and method for the garment.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: A toile (muslin) is typically made during garment construction mainly to
options: permanently line the inside of a finished garment
replace the need for any pattern at all
serve as the final, finished garment itself
test the fit and design of a pattern using cheap fabric before cutting the final garment fabric
questions.explanation: A toile (test garment, often made in muslin) allows a designer to check fit and design details using inexpensive fabric before committing to the final, often costlier, fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: When drafting a basic bodice block, key body measurements typically required include the
options: bust, waist, and back width measurements
shoe size and hat size only
measurements unrelated to the upper body at all
questions.explanation: Drafting an accurate bodice block requires key upper body measurements, such as bust, waist, and back width.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Wardrobe planning that considers weather conditions mainly involves
options: choosing only garments suited to a single season, regardless of location
selecting fabric based solely on colour, with no regard for climate
ignoring climate entirely when selecting garments
selecting fabrics and styles suited to temperature and climate
questions.explanation: Sensible wardrobe planning accounts for climate and weather, selecting appropriate fabric weights and styles for the prevailing conditions.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Age-appropriate clothing selection generally considers factors such as
options: comfort, practicality, and suitability for the wearer's stage of life
ignoring the wearer's age and needs entirely
selecting identical styles for every age group without exception
choosing only the most impractical designs available
questions.explanation: Age-appropriate clothing selection balances comfort, practicality, and suitability, reflecting the specific needs of the wearer's stage of life.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Bleach should generally be used on fabrics only after checking the
options: size label, with no regard for fabric composition
care label, to confirm the fabric can safely tolerate bleach
season in which the garment was purchased
garment's price tag, with no regard for fabric type
questions.explanation: Checking the care label before using bleach helps confirm whether a fabric can safely tolerate this strong chemical treatment, avoiding damage or discolouration.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Protein-based stains, such as blood or egg, are generally best treated initially using
options: cold water, since hot water can set the stain by cooking the protein
direct ironing before any other treatment
boiling hot water, to dissolve the stain quickly
no water of any kind, using only dry heat
questions.explanation: Protein-based stains should generally be treated with cold water first, as hot water can cause the protein to coagulate and set the stain more firmly into the fabric.

questions.subject: Clothing and Textiles
questions.text: Oil-based stains are generally best treated using
options: starch applied directly to the stain
a suitable grease-cutting agent, such as dish soap, before laundering
ignoring the stain entirely, since it will fade naturally
cold water alone, with no other treatment
questions.explanation: Oil-based stains typically respond best to grease-cutting agents, such as dish soap, applied before the garment is laundered.
